title: Karan Johar Unfollowed Shah Rukh Khan, Alia Bhatt, and Nearly Everyone Else on Instagram. He Says It Is a Digital Detox.
excerpt: The filmmaker's mass unfollow triggered speculation about Bollywood rifts. His actual explanation is more mundane — and more relatable than anyone expected.
body:
It started, as these things always do, on Reddit. Someone noticed that Karan Johar's Instagram following count had dropped dramatically. Then the names emerged: Shah Rukh Khan. Alia Bhatt. Kareena Kapoor Khan. Kajol. Malaika Arora. Varun Dhawan. Sidharth Malhotra. Ananya Panday. Kartik Aaryan. Manish Malhotra. And not just the stars themselves — Gauri Khan, Aryan Khan, and Suhana Khan were also gone from his following list.

Within hours, "Karan Johar" was trending. The theories arrived fast: a falling out with Shah Rukh Khan. Professional tensions at Dharma. A feud with Alia Bhatt. Some speculated about the Don 3 controversy and whether the Ranveer Singh–FWICE dispute had fractured relationships across the industry.

The actual explanation, when it came, was almost comically anti-climactic.

## "This Can't Be National News"

Johar addressed the situation on his Instagram Story with the kind of exasperation that suggested he genuinely had not anticipated the reaction. "It's a DIGITAL DETOX!!!! Am unfollowing everyone to reduce my time and energy spent on the gram!!!" he wrote. "This can't be national news for god's sake... please clickbait something else! This is irrelevant!"

The all-caps energy, the four exclamation marks, the plea for the media to find something else to talk about — it was vintage Karan Johar, a man who has spent three decades understanding exactly how Bollywood narratives are constructed and occasionally being frustrated when one is constructed about him.

## Why It Felt Like More Than a Detox

The reason the story traveled so far, so fast, is context. Karan Johar and Shah Rukh Khan's relationship is not just a friendship — it is one of the foundational narratives of modern Bollywood. *Kuch Kuch Hota Hai*, *Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham*, *Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna*, *My Name Is Khan* — Johar has repeatedly credited Khan with shaping his career, his confidence, and his understanding of what cinema can be. An unfollow between the two registers as seismic because the bond itself has been so publicly, so consistently, so emotionally documented.

The inclusion of Alia Bhatt added another layer. She is, by all public accounts, Johar's closest professional protégée and personal friend. He launched her in *Student of the Year*, cast her in multiple Dharma films, and has spoken about her with an affection that goes beyond the typical producer-actor dynamic. Unfollowing her, even as a technical exercise, was always going to generate headlines.

## The Deeper Pattern

This is not the first time Johar has mass-unfollowed on social media. In 2020, following the backlash after Sushant Singh Rajput's death, he pared his Twitter following down to just eight accounts — four Dharma-related, plus Amitabh Bachchan, Shah Rukh Khan, Akshay Kumar, and Narendra Modi. That was widely interpreted as a retreat under pressure. This time, the context is different, but the pattern is the same: a filmmaker who operates in public struggling with how much of his life should remain there.

For the diaspora watching from abroad, the episode is a useful reminder of how Bollywood's social infrastructure works. In an industry where a follow, a like, or an Instagram Story tag carries real professional weight, an unfollow is never just an unfollow. It is a signal, a statement, or at the very least, a story. Karan Johar knows this better than anyone. Which is precisely why his frustration at the coverage is both understandable and slightly disingenuous — he has spent decades building the very ecosystem that now reads his Instagram activity as front-page news.

## What Hasn't Changed

The important thing, which can be lost in the noise: nothing has actually changed. Johar and Shah Rukh Khan continue to work together. Dharma Productions remains one of the most active studios in Hindi cinema. Alia Bhatt's relationship with the Dharma ecosystem is intact. The unfollow is a social media action, not a professional or personal rupture. But the speed at which the story moved — from Reddit observation to national trend to filmmaker clarification within a single news cycle — tells you everything about the parasocial intensity of Bollywood fandom in 2026.

Karan Johar wanted less time on Instagram. He got more of it.
